deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck has diagnosed a defect of crystalline cohomology over W = W(k), which is built from projective limits of p-adically complete objects. On an affine scheme the projective limit does not commute with inverting p (W -> W[1/p] = K), so crystalline cohomology of non-proper (e.g. affine) varieties is badly behaved rationally. He therefore proposes a larger site of 'pro-infinitesimal thickenings' built from Washnitzer-Monsky objects. An object is a triple (U_0, V, i). Here U_0 is an affine open of X_0 with ring A_0. V = 'Spf' of a Washnitzer-Monsky algebra B over W, that is, a weakly complete finitely generated (dagger) W-algebra. i is given by a surjective W-homomorphism B -> A_0 such that B/pB -> A_0 has nilpotent kernel, so U_0 is a nilpotent thickening of the special fibre of V. The topology is a Zariski-type one generated by traces of opens of X_0.

This page states the 'decisive tests' such a theory must pass.
(a) If X_0 is smooth (and affine) over k, the cohomology of this site must reproduce Washnitzer-Monsky cohomology: the de Rham cohomology of a dagger lift A^dagger, tensored with Q.
(b) If X_0 is smooth and proper and lifts to a smooth proper X over S = Spf W, the cohomology must give H_DR(X/S), at least modulo torsion.

He then calls this a first approximation. Even if it works it will have to be made much more flexible. The meta-remark is partly illegible: roughly, one does not want a cohomology theory without knowing what it is good for, and there will be basic cases to test. He ends: 'Il y a de la joie en perspective !'

In modern terms, this is a programme for a p-adic cohomology that unifies Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology (affine smooth) and crystalline/de Rham cohomology (proper smooth). It is exactly the role later played by Berthelot's rigid cohomology (from about 1983/86). Its site-theoretic incarnation is Le Stum's overconvergent site (2000s), with Ogus's convergent site (1984) as the proper-case analogue. The two tests are precisely the two comparison theorems later proved for rigid cohomology: rigid = MW for smooth affine, and rigid = crystalline tensor Q (= de Rham of a lift) for smooth proper.
errors: The site as defined on the previous page requires B/pB -> A_0 to have nilpotent kernel. This only admits thickenings with the same underlying space as U_0, so it is an infinitesimal/crystalline-type condition rather than Berthelot's tube/overconvergent-neighbourhood condition. For singular X_0 such local objects need not exist, since there may be no dagger lift. One would need embeddings into smooth dagger schemes with non-nilpotent kernel (e.g. a point inside a dagger affine line). This is consistent with his own remark that the definition must be 'beaucoup assouplie'.

Test (a) only makes sense rationally: MW cohomology is defined after tensoring with Q, and integral MW-type cohomology is badly behaved. He states 'modulo torsion' explicitly only in (b), but it is implicitly needed in (a) too.
Test (b) holds rationally (crystalline tensor Q = de Rham of the lift). This is consistent with his 'au moins modulo torsion'; no error.

ideas.what: Replace the crystalline site by a site of Washnitzer-Monsky (weakly complete, dagger) thickenings of affine opens of X_0, with a Zariski-type topology, to get a good rational p-adic cohomology for non-proper varieties.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (rigid cohomology, 1980s); Le Stum (overconvergent site, ~2007-2011); Meredith (weakly formal schemes, 1971); Grosse-Klönne (dagger spaces, 2000)
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); unsure

ideas.what: Decisive tests for the new theory: recover MW cohomology for smooth affine X_0, and recover de Rham cohomology of a smooth proper lift modulo torsion.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorems rigid = MW (smooth affine) and rigid = crystalline tensor Q (smooth proper)

ideas.what: Diagnosis that crystalline cohomology fails for affine varieties because projective limits do not commute with inverting p.
ideas.modern_name: Need for overconvergence / failure of rational crystalline cohomology for open varieties

missed.claim: In 1966-67 Grothendieck explicitly proposed a site-theoretic cohomology built from Washnitzer-Monsky (dagger) thickenings. He fixed as its success criteria precisely the two comparison theorems later established for rigid cohomology. This makes him an unrecorded precursor of Berthelot's rigid cohomology and especially of Le Stum's overconvergent site; the standard history starts with MW (1968) and Berthelot (1980s).
missed.quote: Tests décisifs : a) Si X_0 lisse affine sur k, on doit retrouver la définition de W.M. b) Si X_0 lisse et propre, et se relève en X lisse et propre, on doit retrouver (au moins modulo torsion) la cohomologie de De Rham H_DR(X/S).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution: the 'unify MW and crystalline' programme is usually dated to Berthelot circa 1980. The specific design is also notable: a crystalline-style nilpotent-mod-p condition combined with dagger algebras. It is a hybrid of Ogus's convergent site and Le Stum's overconvergent site, which might be of interest to people studying site-theoretic definitions of rigid cohomology.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics was later fully realised (rigid cohomology, overconvergent site), so nothing is mathematically new. But an explicit 1966-67 Grothendieck proposal of a dagger-thickening site, with exactly the right comparison tests, is a notable and probably undocumented precursor.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'lisse' in test (a) reads 'affine' (no question mark needed).

Second paragraph: 'première [...] approximation. Même si elle réussit, il faudra beaucoup l'assouplir' is plausible. The following line is uncertain; possibly 'on ne désire une théorie cohomologique sans connaître le profit' or similar, and should be marked illegible rather than fixed.
Final sentence 'Il y a de la joie en perspective !' is correct.
